SEC Clears Nasdaq’s State Rule Revision; SOL and XRP Included in Digital Commodity Definition

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has approved Nasdaq’s submission of a rules amendment application, with Order No. 34-106268. The core of this revision is the addition of a “digital commodity” definition in Nasdaq Rule 5711(d). Following Bitcoin and Ethereum, Solana and XRP are also explicitly included in this definition, and operating restrictions for commodity trust shares are simultaneously loosened. In the order document, the SEC cites trust products that include these four assets as examples, listing them as “digital commodities” that currently meet the relevant conditions.

Based on the rule details, the new rule allows certain assets that have not met existing listing standards to be included in the portfolio of commodity trust products, but limits their share to no more than 15% of the fund’s net asset value (NAV). This means there is now a more flexible “gap” between the previously clear-cut boundary of assets that do and do not meet listing requirements, giving asset management institutions more room in structuring products. The market expects that the allocation status of XRP and Solana in subsequent compliant investment products may further move closer to Bitcoin and Ethereum—though this is speculation and expectation rather than an established fact.

The boundary must be clearly drawn: this approval applies only to the amendment of Nasdaq’s exchange rules, and does not mean that the federal regulatory layer has formally categorized XRP or Solana within the commodity regulatory regime. It is not a nationwide, unified legal framework, and it does not constitute direct approval for any specific XRP or Solana ETF. Whether later products can be launched and whether the relevant assets can be listed still depends on additional review requirements and processes.

Now, consider the market impact pathway. Fueled by policy expectations, risk appetite has visibly rebounded: over the past 24 hours, total forced liquidations across the market were about $567 million, of which short liquidations were about $479 million, accounting for the vast majority—showing a fairly clear short-squeeze characteristic. Total market capitalization for cryptocurrencies rose to about $2.71 trillion. Flows were also active: U.S. Bitcoin spot ETFs saw net inflows of approximately $731 million on the day, with IBIT leading at about $454 million; Ethereum spot ETFs saw net inflows of about $141 million on the same day; the XRP spot ETF has recorded net inflows for 11 consecutive trading days, with cumulative scale reaching $1.68 billion; and the amount of the stablecoin RLUSD issued on the XRP Ledger surpassed $1 billion. It should be noted that the above figures reflect the market’s overall condition, and the rule revision is only one of the influencing factors. On the macro side, statements by Fed Governor Waller—about slowing inflation and support for keeping interest rates unchanged at the mid-September policy meeting—are also seen as factors supporting risk assets.

Editor’s observation: the real significance of this revision lies in institutional flexibility at the product-structure level, not in a final “regulatory characterization” verdict. Looking ahead, two key points are worth tracking: first, the Senate plans to hold a final vote on ending the CLARITY Act on the 15th; if it passes, the digital asset regulatory framework may become even clearer. Second, whether asset management firms will use the 15% exception quota to file new product applications. Ripple CEO Garlinghouse said that the U.S. becoming “the global crypto hub” is within reach, provided the final wrap-up of the regulatory system is completed. Whether compliance coverage can extend from Bitcoin and Ethereum to mainstream assets such as XRP and Solana still needs to be tested by subsequent processes.

content:
SEC放行纳斯达克得州规则修订 SOL与XRP纳入数字商品定义

美国证券交易委员会（SEC）已批准纳斯达克得州提交的规则修订申请，命令编号为34-106268。此次修订的核心，是在纳斯达克得州规则5711(d)中新增“数字商品”定义：继比特币和以太坊之后，Solana与XRP也被明确纳入该定义，商品型信托股份的运作限制同步放宽。SEC在命令文件中以包含这四种资产的信托产品作为示例，并将它们列为当前符合相关条件的“数字商品”。

从规则细节看，新规允许部分未满足现有上市标准的资产被纳入商品型信托产品组合，但其占基金净资产（NAV）的比例上限为15%。这意味着，过去符合与不符合上市要求之间的明确界限出现了一个弹性口子，资管机构在产品结构安排上获得了更大空间。市场据此预期，XRP与Solana在后续合规投资产品中的配置地位，有望进一步向比特币和以太坊靠拢——这一步属于推测与预期，而非既成事实。

边界必须划清：此次批准仅针对纳斯达克得州交易所规则的修订，并不等同于联邦监管层面已将XRP或Solana正式归入商品监管范畴，不是全美统一的法律框架，也不构成对任何一只XRP或Solana ETF的直接批准。后续具体产品能否落地、相关资产能否上市，仍取决于额外的审核条件与流程。

再看市场影响路径。受政策预期提振，风险偏好明显回升：过去24小时全网强制平仓总额约5.67亿美元，其中空头平仓约4.79亿美元，占绝大部分，呈现较明显的空头挤压特征；加密货币总市值升至约2.71万亿美元。资金面同样活跃，美国比特币现货ETF单日净流入约7.31亿美元，IBIT以4.54亿美元居首；以太坊现货ETF同日净流入约1.41亿美元；XRP现货ETF已连续11个交易日净流入，累计规模增至16.8亿美元；基于XRP账本的稳定币RLUSD供应量突破10亿美元。需要说明，上述数据反映的是市场整体状态，规则修订只是影响因素之一，宏观面上美联储理事沃勒关于通胀放缓、支持9月中旬议息会议维持利率不变的表态，同样被视作支撑风险资产的因素。

编辑观察：这次修订的真正意义，在于产品结构层面的制度弹性，而不是监管定性的最终落锤。往后看，两个节点值得跟踪：一是参议院计划于15日进行的CLARITY法案终结投票，若获通过，数字资产监管框架有望进一步清晰；二是资管机构会否利用15%的例外额度提交新产品申请。Ripple首席执行官加林豪斯称，美国成为“全球加密之都”已近在眼前，前提是完成监管体系的最后收尾。合规覆盖范围能否从比特币、以太坊延伸至XRP、Solana等主流资产，仍需交给后续流程检验。

translatedData.title: Uniswap returns stablecoin arbitrage profits to LPs
translatedData.subTitle:
What’s worth watching isn’t yet another new pool—the fee rules themselves have changed.

Uniswap Labs announced on September 10: the StablePair Hook has launched on the Ethereum mainnet, with the first two pools—$USDC/$USDG and $USDC/$USDT. Official figures: for stablecoin pair swaps, Uniswap’s single platform did $43.4 billion in Q2; that’s more than the combined on-chain volumes of the next three contenders.

The old logic was straightforward: when the price deviated, an arbitrage bot would capture most of the spread. If the fee was set low, the bot took it; if it was set high, the pool priced itself out and got eliminated. StablePair is replaced with dynamic fees: around a reference price, users in the band get a fixed buy-sell price difference; outside the band there’s no charge, and correction moves through a Dutch auction (the fee decays by blocks), with the extra portion kept for LPs.

title: 🚨 $BTC Drops From $82K on Fed Fear — Here's Why I'm Fading the Hike Narrative
subTitle:
🚨 $BTC Drops From $82K on Fed Fear — Here's Why I'm Fading the Hike Narrative

Bitcoin has slid off its $82K high this week, and the reason isn't a hack, a regulatory headline, or an exchange blowup — it's the Federal Reserve. 📉

The market is currently pricing in roughly a coin-flip probability of a 25 basis point rate hike at the upcoming FOMC decision. That uncertainty alone has been enough to knock BTC lower, as leveraged longs de-risk ahead of a binary macro event. When the outcome of a single meeting can move an asset this violently, smart positioning matters more than conviction.

## 🧠 My Read: Rates Hold, Not Hike

I'm taking the other side of the crowd here. My base case is that the Fed **holds rates steady** rather than delivering a surprise hike. A handful of reasons back this view:

- Cooling inflation prints over recent months reduce the urgency to tighten further
- A hawkish surprise this late in the cycle risks overtightening into a slowing labor market
- Historically, the Fed has preferred signaling through language (forward guidance) rather than shock moves when data is mixed

None of this is a guarantee — Fed meetings are famous for wrong-footing consensus — but the risk/reward on a "hold" outcome looks favorable from where BTC is trading right now. ⚖️

## 📊 Two Scenarios I'm Watching

**Scenario 1 — No Hike (my base case):**
If the Fed holds, expect a relief bounce off this dip. Shorts covering + sidelined buyers stepping back in could push BTC back toward recent highs fairly quickly. This is the classic "priced-in fear, doesn't happen" bounce.

**Scenario 2 — Surprise Hike:**
If the Fed actually raises 25bps, expect BTC to retest the $78K support zone, and likely break lower short-term as risk assets reprice for a tighter liquidity environment. Leverage gets flushed, and momentum traders pile on the downside.

## 🎯 How I'm Positioned

This is a textbook **binary event trade** — there's no fence-sitting once the decision drops. I'm positioned for the no-hike outcome, but I'm not romanticizing this trade:

- Entry aligned with the no-hike thesis
- Stop-loss tight, below $79.5K
- No averaging down if Powell surprises to the hawkish side

The stop isn't optional. Binary events are exactly where undisciplined traders get wrecked — you can be right on the macro thesis and still lose money if you're not managing risk going into the print. 🛡️

## ⚡ Key Takeaway

Fed week trades aren't about being a hero — they're about having a thesis, sizing it correctly, and respecting your invalidation level. I believe the hold scenario is underpriced right now, but I'm not staying in this trade if $79.5K breaks. Protect capital first, be right second.

Ethereum is once again testing the patience of bulls. **$ETH** is trending toward a candle close below the trending dots — a setup eerily similar to what **$BTC** printed just yesterday before its own leg down. When two major assets start mirroring each other's structure like this, it's rarely a coincidence, and traders are paying close attention. 👀

 📊 The Current Picture

Looking at the **ETHUSDT Perpetual** chart:

- 💰 Current Price: **$2,447.32**
- 🔻 24H Change: **-0.78%**
- 📉 Momentum: Choppy, rolling over near recent highs

The price action shows a series of weak upward pushes followed by rejection — a classic sign of exhaustion after a mini relief rally. The red candle trend on the mini-chart tells its own story: sellers are stepping back in every time buyers try to reclaim control. 🐻

 ⚠️ The Big Level Everyone's Watching: $2,200

Here's where it gets interesting. There's a **large liquidation cluster sitting at $2,200**, and multiple factors are lining up around this zone, creating what many are calling the "yellow target box" 🟡 on the chart.

Why does this level matter so much?

1. 🎯 **Liquidity Magnet** — Large clusters of leveraged positions tend to act like magnets for price. Markets often gravitate toward zones where the most liquidations can be triggered.
2. 📐 **Technical Confluence** — When a liquidation zone lines up with a trending-dot breakdown, it strengthens the case for a deeper move rather than a quick bounce.
3. 🔗 **Bitcoin Correlation** — With $BTC already showing a similar candle close below its own trending dots, $ETH could simply be following the leader with a short lag.

 🤔 How Many Targets Get Hit?

This is the million-dollar question every trader is asking right now. A few scenarios worth considering:

- **Scenario A – Full Sweep 🌊**: Price breaks below the trending dots cleanly, sweeps liquidity down toward $2,200, triggers the liquidation cascade, and potentially wicks lower before any recovery.
- **Scenario B – Partial Fill ⚖️**: Price dips toward the yellow box, clears some of the liquidity, but finds support before reaching the full $2,200 level.
- **Scenario C – Fakeout Reversal 🔄**: The dots break is a trap, price reclaims the trendline, and shorts get squeezed instead.

Given the mirrored setup with Bitcoin, Scenario A or B currently look more probable — but as always, **confirmation matters more than prediction**. Watch for a clean close below the dots as the trigger, not just a wick.

🧠 Trader Takeaway

- Keep $2,200 firmly on your radar as the key downside magnet 📍
- Watch how $BTC behaves first — ETH is following its script closely 🔁
- Manage leverage carefully; liquidation zones cut both ways ⚔️
- Don't chase the move — let the level come to price, not the other way around 🧘

Index 69 is still within the Greed zone. Drops in the Fear zone (below 25) are about killing sentiment—the more it falls, the more people are afraid, leading to stop-loss cutting and stampedes. In contrast, a drop in the Greed zone is more like profit-taking, with chips moving from weaker hands to stronger hands. In plain terms: yes, it’s down—but holders haven’t been scared out. **2. 69 is a delicate spot: hot, but not overheated**

Above 70 counts as Extreme Greed. Right now it’s stuck at 69, meaning sentiment is hot, but not crazy. What you truly need to worry about is if sentiment and price both collapse together—and based on what we see, that doesn’t look like this scenario.

If the index quickly drops from 69 to below 50, and at the same time the price keeps grinding lower (bearish, drifting down), that would be a true resonance between sentiment and price weakness. According to Crypto Briefing, Trump’s advisory team privately warned that the U.S.-Iran conflict may last until the end of the current term. That means short-term military friction will no longer be “fight and then talk,” but a prolonged drain. The most direct transmission to the crypto market is: a diplomatic solution remains elusive → market risk appetite keeps contracting → rebuilding capital (including previously hyped Middle East infrastructure/crypto collaboration projects) is pushed back entirely.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

Put simply, the market previously priced this conflict as a “short-term event,” with negotiations expected to cool it within a month. Now the advisors are hinting it could drag on for years—so the pricing logic needs to be rewritten. A long-term conflict means oil prices stay elevated, the slowdown in inflation is delayed, and the Fed’s rate-cut window gets pushed back again and again. Each link in this chain is a siphon for risk assets.

BTC is now $78,331.93 (24h -1.04%), ETH $2,477.23 (-1.29%). It’s not a brutal drop, but look at altcoins: BNB -4.30%, SOL -2.30%, XRP -3.33%. The typical high-beta names die first, while BTC holds relatively steadier—funds are withdrawing from tail assets toward the core.

One-sentence translation: This isn’t panic selling—it’s a precautionary liquidity contraction as the market re-prices the conflict as becoming long-term.

Market impact

The transmission path is very specific: geopolitical conflict becomes protracted → safe-haven capital returns to U.S. Treasuries and gold → marginal buying (like ETFs) slows → BTC faces pressure, and altcoins bleed even more. As a reference, during the early 2020 phase when U.S.-Iran tensions escalated, BTC initially tracked the decline in risk assets; the “safe-haven” narrative would only kick in when the conflict truly gets out of control.

Trading outlook

Solana captures a 12% share of the RWA market—so why is the coin price still stuck at $101?
Allium report: Solana accounts for 12% of the on-chain tokenized RWA market value, but the SOL price hasn’t caught up.

According to the Solana RWA ecosystem report released by Allium on September 8 (as relayed by ChainCatcher), over the 12 months up to August 18, 2026, Solana’s on-chain RWA spot trading volume was $14.7 billion with 42.6 million trades. Across the whole chain, the totals were about $46 billion and 91 million trades.

In plain terms: trading volume is about 32%, the number of trades is nearly 47%, yet the market value share is only 12%. One-sentence translation: retail traders are very active trading RWA on Solana, but large holders’ custody assets are still sitting on other chains.

Impact on the market
- Short term: A narrative-level positive for SOL, but today the broader tape is weak (BTC $77,994.88, SOL $101.07 down 2.43%). The report alone can’t move the price—this is the kind of good news where “the data looks great and the wallet is honest.”
- Medium term: If the trading volume share continues to stay higher than the market value share, it suggests that the flow comes first and the assets follow. In the RWA narrative, Solana’s position will become harder to ignore.

My take
Slightly bullish with a neutral tilt. The figure of 47% share of trade count has more substance than the 12% market value share—activity is a leading indicator for market cap. But in the short term, SOL still moves with the overall market; if support around $101 breaks, nothing in the report will matter. I have about a 70% confidence in this view; the remaining 30% depends on how the broader market behaves. For now, I’m only watching with a small position.

🏛️ U.S.-China trade truce hits as a positive catalyst—why is BTC still stuck around 78K?

💡 Impact assessment: Bullish, but slow-burn—business confidence repair comes first; price action lags. Look for a mild rebound within 12 hours.

📊 Quick data check
- BTC: $78,126.01 (24h -0.83%)
- ETH: $2,465.03 (24h -1.25%)
- News sentiment: The U.S.-China trade truce improves business confidence notably in both countries

🔍 Market interpretation
The news itself is genuinely bullish: easing tariff pressure → renewed expectations for cross-border corporate capex → improved macro risk appetite. Historically, in such “trade-smoothing” scenarios, the rally is often first reflected in U.S. stocks and Asian equities, with crypto typically lagging by 1–2 trading days.

Impact on BTC: BTC is still drifting lower at around $78,126, suggesting the market has already priced in part of the trade news. If, over the next 12 hours, BTC can reclaim 78.5K, it would confirm the bullish effect. If it breaks below 77.5K, it means the funds simply aren’t buying it.

Impact on ETH: ETH ($2,465) is underperforming the broader market (-1.25%). Macro bullishness transmits to ETH more slowly; over the next 24 hours, it’s likely to follow up, not lead.

Predicted fund flows: When risk appetite rebounds, it usually lifts altcoins and tech stocks first. BTC benefits, but with limited elasticity. In simple terms: it loosens conditions for the market—not a shot of adrenaline.

💡 Trading suggestion
I’m slightly biased bullish, but I wouldn’t chase with heavy size. In this kind of macro tailwind, moves are slow and pullbacks are also slow. I’d just try a 20% position break near 78.5K; if wrong, I’d cut losses cleanly. My confidence in this call is 70%; the remaining 30% is left to the market.
